name: Clever Impersonator copying Birthing Pod -> a second, independent Birthing Pod chain

prerequisites.mana_available: {2}{U}{U} to cast Clever Impersonator, entering as a copy of a Birthing Pod already on the battlefield. Each Pod activation afterward separately costs {1}{G/P}, tap, sacrifice a creature.
prerequisites.timing: Clever Impersonator's copy choice happens as it enters (a replacement effect, CR 707); each Pod's own activated ability is sorcery-speed only ('Activate only as a sorcery', confirmed in Birthing Pod's Oracle text).
other: NOT a combo/loop in the Commander Spellbook sense - checked (query for card="Birthing Pod" card="Clever Impersonator" together) and Spellbook returns zero variants. This is a redundancy/resilience finding, not a win-condition line: two independently-sacrificeable, independently-activatable Birthing Pods let the deck sacrifice two creatures per turn (mana permitting) instead of one, and survive losing one Pod to removal without losing the effect entirely.

CORRECTION (2026-08-12, caught by user review): Clever Impersonator's own oracle text is only 'You may have this creature enter as a copy of any nonland permanent on the battlefield.' It does NOT itself say anything like 'becomes an artifact in addition to its other types' - that was a factual error in an earlier draft of this record. The reason the resulting permanent IS an artifact is CR 707.2: when copying an object, the copy acquires the copiable values of the original's characteristics, and card type is one of those copiable values. Birthing Pod's own printed card type is Artifact, so Clever Impersonator, having chosen to copy it, acquires 'Artifact' as part of that copy - the type comes entirely from what was copied, not from any type-adding clause on Clever Impersonator itself.
Birthing Pod is not legendary (type line is plain 'Artifact'), so no legend rule conflict between the original and the copy.

Relevant to Phase 4 (combo dependency graph, as a redundancy/bridge node) and Phase 26 (combo accessibility - Clever Impersonator is a generic 'copy the best permanent on the battlefield' effect, not specific to Pod; Pod is simply one of several high-value copy targets alongside Smothering Tithe (INT-0001), and potentially Kinnan, Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, or Survival of the Fittest depending on board state - not all enumerated here).

VERIFICATION SCOPE (2026-08-12, per docs/VERIFICATION_LEVELS.md, corrected after user review flagged that the original writeup conflated a downstream-consequence test with a full exact reproduction): the executable_engine_check below tests two literal Birthing Pod permanents, NOT the actual 'Clever Impersonator enters, chooses to copy Birthing Pod, becomes Birthing Pod' transition this interaction is named for. That exact transition was attempted and could not be made to run reliably through this project's test harness (see notes) and has NOT been engine-reproduced. What IS engine-verified is the downstream consequence the copy would produce if it succeeded: two Pod-functioning permanents can each be independently activated in the same turn. Combined with the CR 707.1/707.2 citations establishing the copy mechanism itself is rules-legal and produces a functioning Birthing Pod copy, this interaction is ENGINE_COMPONENT_VERIFIED, not ENGINE_EXACT_VERIFIED - see verification_level and docs/VERIFICATION_LEVELS.md for what that distinction permits and forbids downstream.

result.summary: A second, independently activatable Birthing Pod - increases sacrifice-outlet redundancy and mana-permitting throughput (2 creatures sacrificed/found per turn instead of 1), not a new win condition by itself.

rules_citations: CR 707.1 — some objects become or turn another object into a 'copy' of a permanent; Clever Impersonator's own ability is this kind of effect.

CR 707.2 — when copying an object, the copy acquires the copiable values of the original's characteristics (card type among them), including rules text (which includes its activated abilities). This is why Clever Impersonator, having copied Birthing Pod, genuinely has Birthing Pod's own sacrifice-and-search activated ability AND Birthing Pod's own Artifact card type - both are copied values, neither is added by Clever Impersonator's own printed text.

General activated-ability rules (CR 602) place no restriction preventing two non-legendary permanents with the same activated ability from each being activated once in the same turn, as long as each pays its own cost independently (here, its own tap + sacrifice + mana) - confirmed by the absence of any 'activate only once per turn' style restriction in Birthing Pod's Oracle text (its only restriction is 'Activate only as a sorcery').

executable_engine_check.notes: IMPORTANT: this run does NOT reproduce Clever Impersonator's own copy transition. It reproduces a downstream consequence of it instead - see the verification-scope note in prerequisites.other and docs/VERIFICATION_LEVELS.md. Reproduced in the same from-source Maven build of magefree/mage (JDK 21) used for the rest of this project's Level 4 work, via a new JUnit test, org.mage.test.cards.interactions.cedh.CleverImpersonatorBirthingPodTest#test_TwoBirthingPods_BothIndependentlyActivatable (not committed to this repo — see docs/RUN_CLASSIFICATION.md and rules_tests/gold_board_states/GBS-0009.json for the fixture record). Test setup: two literal Birthing Pod permanents (a stand-in for 'original + Clever Impersonator's copy', NOT a reproduction of the copy step itself), 2 Elvish Mystic (sac fodder), 4 Forest, and 2 Silvercoat Lion in the library, for playerA. Activated BOTH Pod abilities in the same main phase, one after the other. Result: both Elvish Mystic sacrificed, both Silvercoat Lion found, both Pods remain on the battlefield afterward - confirming the downstream 'two independently-activatable Pods' consequence, not the copy transition that would produce it. Getting even this component test to run cleanly required a real methodology finding: this project's normal setChoice/addTarget queue-based approach for cost-payment choices (sacrifice target, Phyrexian mana pay-or-decline) does NOT work reliably for this activateAbility() call shape - the framework's own source comment on that overload states cost-payment 'choices and targets commands aren't [supported]' and instead routes through an internal computerPlayer AI fallback. Multiple attempts using setChoice/addTarget for the sacrifice target and Phyrexian choice failed unpredictably ('Missing CHOICE def' / 'wrong choice command' errors that didn't resolve with reordering) both for this test AND for an earlier attempt at the actual cast-and-copy sequence, which is why that exact sequence was not pursued further and this component test was substituted instead. Fix for the component test: dropped setStrictChooseMode, let the AI fallback resolve the cost (it has no real choice to make here - only 1 legal sacrifice target type and only 1 legal search target existed at each step), and controlled nothing but the initial board setup. Passed 1/1 once restructured this way.

sources.reference: Independent reasoning about Clever Impersonator's copy ability against Birthing Pod's own text, cross-checked against Commander Spellbook's variants index (zero results for the pair, confirming this is not a community-tracked combo - a redundancy finding, not a missed win line).
